## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sumaṅgalamātātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.3) is a short verse text located in the *Therīgāthā* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The verses are attributed to the nun Sumaṅgalamātā, who meditates happily reflecting upon her attainment of liberation [Anālayo, From Craving to Liberation]. Later scholarship on early Buddhist communities notes her origin as both the daughter and wife of workers in rushes, highlighting the diverse social backgrounds of early converts [Rhys Davids, Dialogues of the Buddha], and situates her among the prominent bhikkhunīs and female lay followers associated with Sāvatthī [Nakamura, Gotama Buddha].
